summary: A target-level plan for Saito Hodge modules, their exponential quotient and the irregular Hodge filtration used by the Kloosterman appendix. General D-module algebra is imported from the Springer roadmap. The plan fixes Betti, cohomological, Tate and weight conventions, supplies the classical tg criterion and the general log/Newton computational interfaces, and keeps the special Kloosterman computations with their companion owner.

nodes.title: Algebraically constructible Betti complexes
nodes.statement: For a separated finite-type complex variety X, let Dᵇ_c(X_an,Q) be the full subcategory of the derived category of sheaves of Q-vector spaces whose cohomology is bounded, finite dimensional on stalks and locally constant on a finite algebraic Whitney stratification. Construct f*, Rf_*, Rf_!, f!, derived tensor, internal Hom, external product and Verdier duality for algebraic maps, with adjunctions, proper base change, projection formula and the two open/closed localization triangles. Do the same over C and compare by Q→C. Define RΓ_Z by i_*i! for a closed support Z.
hypotheses: All maps are algebraic; coefficient fields are Q and C.
Constructibility of a nonproper analytic direct image is not asserted.
proofSteps: Apply the EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E1 nodes for ringed topoi to the topological space X_an (from the ComplexComparisonPartII:C0/repair-analytification carrier) with constant coefficient rings Q and C: they give the derived categories, Lf*=f⁻¹ and Rf_*, derived tensor, internal Hom and coefficient change; take the full bounded constructible subcategories.

Choose compatible algebraic Whitney stratifications for a map and use stratified local triviality to prove finite constructibility of direct images (the stratification theorem is gap G5); construct Rf_! by proper supports and f! as its right adjoint (Verdier duality), and verify the adjunctions.
Prove localization on an open/closed pair and proper base change stalkwise, then derive support cohomology and Künneth from the projection formula.

nodes.statement: For an algebraic Whitney stratification and a smooth complex stratum S of dimension s, define the middle perverse t-structure by Hʲ(i_S*K)=0 for j>−s and Hʲ(i_S!K)=0 for j<−s. Prove independence of the adapted stratification, boundedness and self-duality; its heart Perv(X,Q) is abelian. Construct perverse cohomology and j_!*L=image(pH⁰j_!L→pH⁰Rj_*L). For a local system L on a smooth d-fold, L[d] is perverse. Constants on a reduced divisor in a smooth variety are perverse after the divisor-dimension shift.
hypotheses: Use finite algebraic constructibility from B/constructible-six-operations; the normal-slice description of strata uses the stratification input of gap G5.
The reduced divisor is a local complete intersection; no assertion for arbitrary singular constants is made.
proofSteps: Glue the support and cosupport truncations over strata, using open/closed recollement from B/constructible-six-operations.
Check independence by refinement, and exchange the inequalities with Verdier duality.
Use normal slices and the local complete-intersection connectivity bound to prove the reduced-divisor constant case; form images in the glued heart.

Set pψ_f=Rψ_f[−1] and pφ_f=Rφ_f[−1]. Prove t-exactness on perverse objects, finite monodromy decomposition after complexification and the can/var triangles. On the generalized eigenvalue-one part normalize variation by the invertible series log(T)/(T−1) so that var∘can=N=(2πi)⁻¹log T_u after adjoining the Tate line; the unnormalized topological relation is var_top∘can=T−1.

nodes.title: Regular algebraic Riemann–Hilbert comparison
nodes.statement: For X a smooth complex algebraic d-fold, analytification followed by pDR(M)=DR(M)[d] identifies algebraic regular holonomic left D_X-modules with algebraically constructible complex perverse sheaves. Extend to bounded derived categories with regular holonomic cohomology. The comparison is exact, fully faithful and compatible with the six operations, duality and tensor/external product. Compatibility with nearby and vanishing cycles is not part of this node: it is proved at H.0/v-filtration (Sai88 Proposition 3.4.12) from the V-filtration. Regularity includes regular singularities at an algebraic compactification boundary. The inverse is the regular holonomic realization of the constructible complex, not arbitrary analytic solutions of an irregular connection.
hypotheses: Regularity and D-module six operations are the Springer-owned notions.
Unshifted DR has terms in degrees 0,…,d.
proofSteps: Use the tempered-solution construction in Kash84 §6 to define an inverse on constructible complexes.

Reduce local biduality and regularity to a local system on the complement of a normal-crossing divisor by embedded resolution and principalization (AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry:R09.7), proper direct image and induction on support; solve the normal-crossing logarithmic model; on the smooth locus the base case is Deligne's regular-singular equivalence (ComplexComparisonPartII C5/deligne-regular-singular-equivalence).
Verify the adjunction maps locally, glue them, and algebraize the regular meromorphic extension. Translate the solution comparison to pDR by holonomic duality and verify the displayed shift.

nodes.title: Formal differential modules and irregularity
nodes.statement: At a chosen coordinate x on a smooth complex curve, a formal differential module is a finite-dimensional C((x))-vector space V with a C-linear connection ∂ satisfying ∂(av)=a′v+a∂v. A lattice is a free C[[x]]-submodule spanning V. Regular singular means some lattice is stable under D=x∂. Define intrinsic irregularity by χ(D:E→E₁)+dim_C(E₁/E), for lattices E⊂E₁ with DE⊂E₁, where χ is dimension of kernel minus dimension of cokernel. Prove finiteness, independence of the lattice pair and coordinate, nonnegativity, additivity in exact sequences, and vanishing precisely at regular singularity.
hypotheses: Finite rank and characteristic zero; all lattice quotients have finite complex dimension.
proofSteps: Form the differential-module category over the pinned LaurentSeries C=C((x)) with its lattice ring PowerSeries C=C[[x]], and the ramified scalar extension x=uᵉ by substitution; compare with Springer’s algebraic connections on a curve only at D/curve-index.
Use a cyclic vector to produce one lattice pair with a finite-index operator. Compare two pairs through a common larger pair and their finite-dimensional quotient exact sequences.
Apply the lattice-index comparison to prove additivity, nonnegativity, the stable-lattice criterion and coordinate invariance, without using the exponential decomposition.

nodes.title: Ramified exponential decomposition
nodes.statement: Every formal differential module over C((x)) admits, after some finite ramification x=uᵉ, a decomposition into E^φ⊗R_φ with φ in u⁻¹C[u⁻¹] and R_φ regular singular. The distinct exponential factors are unique up to the ramification action, and there are no horizontal homomorphisms between different exponential factors. Consequently the groups of equal rational slope descend canonically and are independent of e. Define the rational slope of E^φ⊗R_φ as pole_u(φ)/e, with zero slope for φ=0. The rank-weighted slope sum equals the intrinsic irregularity of D/formal-differential-module, is integral, and is independent of the splitting ramification.
hypotheses: Finite rank over the characteristic-zero Laurent-series field.
proofSteps: Choose a cyclic vector and normalize the matrix; split distinct leading eigenvalues by recursive off-diagonal gauge elimination.
In the nilpotent-leading case perform the Turrittin–Katz shearing and finite ramification of Mal22 §9.E; the rank or irregularity induction terminates.

Remove each scalar negative Laurent principal part by an exponential factor and finish with a stable logarithmic lattice. Prove uniqueness by the leading term of a putative horizontal Hom, then descend slope groups.
Compare the lattice index on each elementary factor and under ramification to identify the intrinsic invariant with the normalized slope sum.

nodes.title: Index and punctual extension on G_m
nodes.statement: Let E be an algebraic connection on G_m whose singularity at zero is regular. Its algebraic de Rham groups are finite dimensional, vanish outside degrees zero and one, and dim H¹_dR(G_m,E)−dim H⁰_dR(G_m,E)=irr_∞(E). More generally the connection Euler characteristic on a smooth open curve is rank(E)χ_c(U)−Σ_boundary irr_x(E). For j:G_m→A¹, ker(j_!E→j_!*E) and coker(j_!*E→j_*E) have support {0}. The assertion about punctual support does not imply their cohomology vanishes.
hypotheses: The index uses unshifted DR.
The general formula sums over the complete smooth boundary; the G_m specialization uses irr_0=0.
proofSteps: Use the smooth projective completion (SF.3/nonsingular-projective-model) and the place expansions at boundary points (AlgebraicCurves Layer 9) to pass to formal differential modules; the meromorphic lattice comparison reduces the global Euler characteristic to that of a pair of coherent lattices on the completion.
Apply curve Riemann–Roch (SF.3/vector-bundle-riemann-roch) to their degrees and insert the local index defect of Mal20 Theorem 3.3; D/formal-decomposition identifies the defect with the slope sum.
Specialize χ_c(G_m)=0. Restrict the kernel and cokernel of the intermediate-extension maps to G_m and use their zero restriction to obtain punctual support.

nodes.title: Exponential connections and twists
nodes.statement: For U smooth and f a regular function, define E^f=(O_U,d+df), the left D_U-module on which a vector field ξ acts by ξ+ξ(f). Construct M⊗E^f and its meromorphic extension at a pole divisor. Its unshifted de Rham differential is ∇_M+df∧. Identify E^f⊗E^g=E^{f+g}, D(E^f)=E^{−f} and h^+E^f=E^{f∘h}, with the normalized D-module inverse-image convention specified separately. On C[t], the rank-one differential is p↦p′+f′p.
hypotheses: f regular on U; a meromorphic extension explicitly permits poles on the chosen boundary.
Duality of a general twisted module is D(M⊗E^f)=DM⊗E^{−f}.
proofSteps: Define the vector-field action and use the Leibniz and integrability relations of Springer’s D-module algebra to extend it.
Apply the existing tensor/transfer and duality functors; compute the differential and its sign in local coordinates.
For the affine polynomial check use the pinned Polynomial.derivative and derivative_mul, without introducing a new derivative.

nodes.statement: With input coordinate τ and output coordinate t, define FT_τM=p_{t,+}(p_τ^+M⊗E^{tτ}). On the Weyl-algebra realization, t acts as −∂_τ and ∂_t as τ. This is an exact autoequivalence of holonomic modules and an equivalence on bounded holonomic complexes, with FT_tFT_τ≅r_+ for r(τ)=−τ. Goodness means local finite generation over the Rees ring, not arbitrary coherent pieces. Strict filtered morphisms are exactly those whose Rees cokernel has no z-torsion. Side changing to right modules is F_p(M^r)=ω_X⊗F_{p+d}M for d=dim X; weights are unchanged. Define filtered pDR by F_p(pDR M)^j=Ω_X^{j+d}⊗F_{p+j+d}M for −d≤j≤0.

nodes.title: Rational specialization filtration
nodes.statement: For a regular holonomic module, quasi-unipotent along a smooth coordinate x=0, construct its unique increasing rational Kashiwara–Malgrange filtration V_α with coherent V_0D-lattices, exhaustive and locally discrete, xV_α⊂V_{α−1}, ∂_xV_α⊂V_{α+1}, and x∂_x+α nilpotent on gr^V_α. Set gr^V_α=V_α/V_{<α}. For a good F impose x:F_pV_α→F_pV_{α−1} is an isomorphism for α<1, and ∂_x:F_p gr^V_α→F_{p+1}gr^V_{α+1} is an isomorphism for α>0. Define cycles for a general function by its graph direct image; keep the graph’s codimension-one F shift. Compare the appropriate fundamental interval with the normalized Betti cycles.

Quasi-unipotence makes the exponents rational; regularity alone is not that rationality assertion.
Uniqueness follows from the generalized eigenspaces and the shift relations. Translate Saito’s right-module conventions by H.0/filtered-rees.

Construct the graph direct image, compare its graded de Rham complex with Betti nearby cycles (Sai88 Proposition 3.4.12: the de Rham complexes of gr^V_α for α in the fundamental intervals are ψ_{f,λ} and φ_{f,1} of DR M, with x∂_x+α, ∂_x and x matching N, can and var), and transport the F conditions through the graph shift. A function identically zero on a component is handled by its supported/Kashiwara clause, not by a false decrease of support dimension. A polarization is a nondegenerate rational duality M→D M(−w) satisfying the primitive sign and positivity conditions of Saito 5.2.10. Strict support means absence of subobjects and quotients on a smaller closed support. On a smooth d-dimensional support the smooth objects are polarizable rational variations of weight w−d.

nodes.statement: If ΠN^H is classical, there is a natural bifiltered isomorphism (ωN,W,F_irr)≅(φ_{θ,1}N^H)_C with its classical W,F. At rational λ the right-hand filtration is F^{ceil(λ)}. proofSteps: For N=i_{0,*}V use the explicit filtered point direct image F_p=Σ_kF_{p−1−k}V∂^k and compute its two-term twisted de Rham complex.
The filtered complex is quasi-isomorphic to V[−1] with its original F, including the codimension-one shift.

nodes.title: Ordinary, compact and middle cohomology of a pair
nodes.statement: For U smooth quasi-projective of dimension d, f:U→A¹_θ and N^H∈MHM(U), set N_*^r=H^{r−d}f_*N^H, N_!^r=H^{r−d}f_!N^H and N_mid^r=image(N_!^r→N_*^r). Define H^r(U,N^H,f)=ΠN_*^r, H_c^r=ΠN_!^r and H_mid^r=ΠN_mid^r, with their W^E and filtered de Rham fibres. For N^H=pQ_U omit the coefficient. At f=0 identify these objects with the classical mixed Hodge structures of ordinary, compact and image cohomology, with the indicated unshifted DR degrees.
hypotheses: Coefficients are Hodge modules on all of U; a smooth variation is the special case whose left module is a connection.
The shift r−d depends on U even for a supported coefficient.
proofSteps: Apply the Hodge direct images and take the perverse cohomology degree r−d.
Use abelianity for the middle image and exactness of Π to commute it with that image.
For the zero map factor through the point, then use C/classical-embedding and the point equivalence to identify the ordinary cohomological MHS.

The identifications are bifiltered for the pushforward Deligne filtration and exponential weights, and commute with coefficient long exact sequences.
hypotheses: Use unshifted DR degrees and the pushforward filtered realization; compact DR is defined through holonomic ! direct image.
proofSteps: Apply the projection formula for exponential twisting to f_* and f_!.

Use the direct-image spectral sequence and E/de-rham-fibre: the exponential fibre of every perverse cohomology term has cohomology only in degree one, so the spectral sequence has a single nonzero row.

Insert the r−d normalization and exactness of ω and Π; use I/irregular-e1 (the Deligne construction commutes with the projective pushforward of a compactification of f) for the filtered identification, and I/strict-bifiltered-realisation for filtered images.

nodes.title: Künneth and duality for exponential cohomology
nodes.statement: For smooth U,V and regular f,g, the pair (U×V,f⊞g) has H^r=⊕_{a+b=r}H^a(U,f)⊗_E H^b(V,g), and similarly for compact supports, as exponential mixed Hodge structures. W is the integral tensor convolution. For U of dimension d, the natural trace pairing H_c^r(U,f)⊗_E H^{2d−r}(U,−f)→Q(−d) is perfect and compatible with W. The coefficient version uses holonomic dual coefficients with the dimension normalization inherited from H.1. Compatibility with the rational irregular filtration for constant coefficients is the separate log-comparison theorem N/filtered-kunneth-duality.
hypotheses: The dual exponential has sign −f; this sign must not be dropped.
The statement uses the rational de Rham realization; it does not introduce a Betti fibre for arbitrary exponentials.
proofSteps: Use the Hodge external product, projection formula and the exponential tensor E^{f⊞g}=E^f⊠E^g.
Apply Π and the exact monoidal fibre to obtain the Künneth decomposition and its weight compatibility. This does not by itself prove the irregularly filtered formula.
Apply duality to the !/* direct images, with D(pQ_U)=pQ_U(d), and evaluate the exponential factors E^f and E^{−f}; the trace gives the twist (−d).

sources.match: Uses Künneth for the sum of coordinates (convolution powers) and the duality H^jf_!≅(DH^{−j}f_*)(−k) with its Tate twist.
Proves compatibility of duality with the irregular filtration in its logarithmic realization.

nodes.title: Middle degree and the lowest weight piece
nodes.statement: For U smooth of dimension d and constant coefficients, H_c^d(U,f) has exponential weights ≤d, H^d(U,f) has weights ≥d, and H_mid^d(U,f) is pure of weight d. The map gr_d^W H_c^d→gr_d^W H^d is an isomorphism if and only if H_mid^d=W_dH^d. All maps and identifications are strict for F_irr and W.
hypotheses: This is the central degree d and the constant pure coefficient of weight d.
proofSteps: Apply the ! upper and * lower weight bounds to H⁰f_!pQ_U and H⁰f_*pQ_U, then descend by Π.
The image has both bounds, hence is pure of weight d.
Use the kernel/cokernel sequences of !→*, their duality with the Tate twist, and exact gr^WΠ to show that vanishing of the weight-d cokernel is equivalent to vanishing of the weight-d kernel.

If D is smooth, construct …→H^{r−2}(D)(−1)→H^r(U,f)→H^r(U∖D,f)→H^{r−1}(D)(−1)→…, commuting with the compact-to-ordinary comparison. For singular D the ordinary localization triangle retains RΓ_D rather than the smooth purity replacement.
hypotheses: D is reduced; the ordinary displayed sequence requires smooth D.
proofSteps: Apply f_! and Π to H.1/divisor-localisation, and use the dimension normalization and zero-function comparison on D.
For smooth D apply f_* to its other sequence, including its codimension-one Tate twist.
Use naturality of the localization triangles to prove the commutative comparison diagram.

nodes.title: Affine-line and torus-sum examples
nodes.statement: For every r, H^r(A¹,t)=H_c^r(A¹,t)=0. For k≥1, H^r(G_m^k,x₁+⋯+x_k) vanishes except r=k, where it is the classical Q(−k); H_c^r vanishes except r=k, where it is Q(0). The compact-to-ordinary map in degree k is zero and H_mid^k=0. For k=0 the point case is Q in degree zero and its comparison is the identity.
hypotheses: These are equalities in the classical subcategory and hence statements about both Hodge and irregular filtrations.
proofSteps: The affine identity pushforward is constant and is killed by Π.
Use the two divisor sequences at {0} to obtain H¹(G_m,x)=Q(−1) and H_c¹(G_m,x)=Q.
Use Künneth for the k-fold sum and duality for compact supports. The comparison is zero for k≥1 by the different pure weights.

nodes.title: The classical tg criterion
nodes.statement: For V smooth quasi-projective, g∈O(V), M^H∈MHM(V), U=A¹_t×V and f=tg, all H^r(U,pQ_A¹⊠M^H,f) and H_c^r are classical. For pQ_A¹[*0]⊠M^H the ordinary groups are classical in every degree; for pQ_A¹[!0]⊠M^H the compact groups are classical. Their bifiltered fibres are the corresponding ordinary MHS, so F_irr agrees exactly with F. These assertions allow g=0 and an arbitrary singular or empty zero locus.
hypotheses: The one-sided [*0] and [!0] hypotheses are kept in their stated support theories.
proofSteps: Localize along A¹×g⁻¹(0); its supported term pushes to θ=0 and is classical. On the complement push first along (t,g) to reduce to g=τ.

The ordinary localized fibre is the Fourier de Rham complex [M(*0)→M(*0)] with differential multiplication by τ. It is acyclic since τ is invertible. Obtain the compact version by duality with sign involution.

For [*0], replace M by Π_τM; the difference has constant cohomology killed after localization of its Fourier transform. Constancy is checked on underlying D-modules: an admissible mixed Hodge module on A¹ whose underlying local system is constant is constant, by HodgeStructuresPartII H.2/mixed-fixed-part (A¹ is simply connected, so the evaluation of the invariants is a bijective morphism of variations, hence an isomorphism by strictness). Use E/fourier-localisation-projector for the other comparison. Duality gives [!0].
Use faithfulness of the exponential fibre to obtain the classicality statement in EMHS, then C/classical-filtration for its bifiltration.

sources.match: Proves all three classicality cases using localization, Fourier acyclicity and the projector.

acceptance: The argument works with the derived pushforward of M, since the projector and fibre are exact on cohomology.
No tameness or nondegeneracy assumption on g is needed.

nodes.title: Zero-locus description of tg cohomology
nodes.statement: For constant coefficients and K=g⁻¹(0) as a reduced support, identify H_c^r(A¹×V,tg)≅H_c^{r−2}(K)(−1), and H^r(A¹×V,tg)≅H_K^r(V). These are isomorphisms of classical MHS and filtered fibres. If K is a smooth divisor, identify the ordinary group further with H^{r−2}(K)(−1). For g=0 the ordinary group is H^r(V) and the compact group is H_c^{r−2}(V)(−1); for g a unit both groups vanish.
hypotheses: The smooth-divisor clause is not applied to g=0 or a singular K.
The support category handles singular K without requiring it to be smooth.
proofSteps: Use the localized vanishing from G/tg-classicality and the compact localization triangle to reduce compact cohomology to A¹×K, where the exponential function is zero.
Apply compact Künneth with H_c²(A¹)=Q(−1).

For ordinary cohomology use i_*i! and homotopy invariance in the A¹ direction, obtaining supports H_K^r(V). The map tg∘i is the zero-valued function, whose direct image factors through the point; its pushforward functor is not the zero functor. Apply purity only for a smooth divisor.

sources.match: Gives the compact zero-locus and ordinary support formulas; the assertion about a zero pushforward is corrected here.

acceptance: For V=pt and g=0 the groups are Q in ordinary degree zero and Q(−1) in compact degree two.

For a singular K retain H_K^r(V), not a smooth purity formula.

nodes.title: Classical cohomology of a Fourier transform
nodes.statement: For M^H∈MHM(A¹_τ), define the classical MHS H^j(A¹_t,FTM^H)=H^{j+1}(A¹_t×A¹_τ,pQ_A¹⊠M^H,tτ), and similarly H_c^j. Their de Rham fibres are H^j_dR(A¹,FTM) and H^j_dR,c(A¹,FTM); ordinary cohomology can be nonzero only in j=0,1 and compact cohomology only in j=1,2. Give them the F_irr and W supplied by the classical pair comparison. This notation does not assert that FTM is a regular Hodge module.
hypotheses: M^H is the regular input; its Fourier transform may be irregular.
proofSteps: Use G/tg-classicality to define the classical MHS through the pair.
Compare the projection along τ with the Fourier kernel and account for its relative dimension one.
Apply P/pair-fibre and the affine-curve holonomic DR bounds; obtain the compact degree range by duality.

nodes.title: Fourier cohomology is the costalk
nodes.statement: For every M^H∈MHM(A¹_τ), there are natural isomorphisms of classical MHS H^j(A¹_t,FTM^H)≅H^j i_0!M^H for all j. Both sides vanish outside degrees zero and one. The isomorphisms identify W and the irregular Hodge filtration on the Fourier fibre with the classical W,F of the costalk.

proofSteps: First compute M=i_{0,*}V: the tτ pair is supported on θ=0 and gives V in pair degree one.
Apply the localization triangle i_*i!M→M→M[*0]. The Fourier de Rham complex of the last term is acyclic since it becomes multiplication by the invertible input coordinate τ.

If M is nonsingular at zero, this is ψ_τM^H(−1), pure of weight w+1, and dim gr^p_{F_irr}H¹_dR(A¹,FTM)=rank gr_F^{p−1}M for every integer p.
hypotheses: Absence of a punctual summand at zero is weaker than nonsingularity there; the rank formula requires nonsingularity.
proofSteps: Apply T/fourier-costalk and the pure costalk decomposition.
Use pure semisimplicity to rule out a degree-zero costalk when no punctual summand occurs.

For every integer l,p, dim gr^p_{F_irr}gr_l^WH¹_dR(A¹,FTM′)=rank gr_F^{p−1}gr_{l−1}^WM′. Here the left W is the classical cohomology weight and the right W is ambient MHM weight.
hypotheses: The rank formula applies to the constant quotient, which is smooth at zero.
proofSteps: The projector kernel is the maximal constant submodule and hence vanishes. Pure splitting rules out an additional weight-w constant quotient inside ΠM, giving the lower bound.
Apply T/pure-fourier-hodge separately to every pure constant gr_{l−1}^WM′.
Use exact W-graded realization and the shift from a constant curve module to its nearby-cycle MHS.

nodes.title: Regular Fourier stationary phase at eigenvalue one
nodes.statement: For a regular holonomic input M on A¹, including infinity, compare the unipotent vanishing cycles of its Fourier transform at output zero with the unipotent nearby cycles of M at input infinity, intertwining nilpotent monodromy after the Fourier sign normalization. The comparison is natural for the localization map FT(M)→FT(M)(*0) and matches its can/var diagram with ψ_∞M→ψ_∞ΠM. Use the underlying regular local system comparison; filtered Tate shifts are attached through Hodge cycles, rather than claiming the irregular Fourier module is an MHM.
hypotheses: The finite input is regular.
A complete kernel-specialization proof of this local stationary-phase comparison is recorded as gap G3.
proofSteps: Compactify the kernel to P¹×A¹ and specialize at the Fourier coordinate zero.
Use the local exponential model near the input boundary and exclude the nonzero finite exponential factors; identify the surviving unipotent factor and its logarithm.
Apply proper specialization and compare the natural localization/variation morphisms. This is the missing proof input isolated by G3, not a consequence of exactness of Fourier alone.

nodes.title: Monodromy weights at infinity of the projector
nodes.statement: Let M^H be pure polarizable of weight w with no constant submodule, and write 0→M→ΠM→M″→0. Set Ψ=ψ_{∞,1}ΠM and L_kΨ=ψ_{∞,1}(W_{k+1}ΠM). Its weight filtration is the absolute monodromy filtration of N centered at w. On underlying nilpotent vector spaces Im N=ψ_{∞,1}M; the inclusion with its filtration shift is the variation comparison. Write P_k=ker[N^{k+1}:gr^W_{w−1+k}ψ_{∞,1}M→gr^W_{w−3−k}ψ_{∞,1}M(−k−1)] for k≥0. Then W_{w+1}M″ is the constant variation with fibre H⁰(P¹,pDR M_min), and gr^W_{w+k+2}M″ is the constant variation with fibre P_k(−1). M_min is the pure intermediate extension to P¹. Retain every primitive part P_k.
hypotheses: The central weight for ψ∞ΠM is w; for ψ∞M it is w−1.
The statement is general pure input and does not assume a single Jordan block.
proofSteps: Compute the constant quotient from the long exact global sequence and RΓ(ΠM)=0: its constant fibre is H⁰(A¹,pDR M).
Use intermediate extension to P¹ and the boundary coker N to split its weight-graded pieces into H⁰(P¹,pDR M_min) and the primitive parts P_k(−1).
Apply regular Fourier stationary phase and semisimplicity to identify Im N on the projected nearby space with the original nearby space.
Use the primitive decomposition to compare dimensions of the relative and absolute monodromy graded pieces; pure negative pieces and monodromy symmetry force W=M(N)[w].

nodes.title: Logarithmic pole-order complex
nodes.statement: A good compactification of (U,f) is a smooth projective X with D=X∖U a simple normal crossing divisor and f extending to X→P¹; write its pole divisor P with multiplicities and D=P_red+T. Define the decreasing rational filtered twisted log complex by (F^λ_logDR_f)^q=0 for q<λ and Ω_X^q(log D)(floor((q−λ)P)) for q≥λ, with differential d+df∧. Its λ≤0 underlying quasi-isomorphism recovers DR(U,E^f). For compact supports use the log complex twisted by O(−T), retaining the pole components instead of twisting by all of D. Also allow a non-degenerate compactification whose local indeterminacy model is f=z/x^e, with zero and pole divisors transverse, in addition to the pole model 1/x^e.
hypotheses: P is the effective pole divisor with its actual multiplicities.
The compact support model has the induced rational filtration and the horizontal boundary twist −T.
proofSteps: Obtain a good model from an SNC compactification of U (R09.7/snc-compactification) by principalizing the indeterminacy ideal of f (R09.7/principalization), so that f extends to X→P¹ with SNC boundary.
Check that d+df∧ preserves the displayed degree-dependent pole bounds; use the local exponential Koszul calculation to compare the meromorphic and log complexes.
Define the compact variant through extension by zero at the horizontal boundary and meromorphic extension at poles; compare with holonomic ! de Rham realization.

nodes.title: Filtered comparison under the toric blowups
nodes.statement: For the explicit blowup resolving an indeterminacy stratum of the non-degenerate model f=z/x^e, the pullback comparison of F^λ_log complexes is a filtered derived isomorphism after pushforward, for every rational λ. In Yu’s interpolation between the pulled-back complex and the complex of the new pole divisor, the successive error terms are sums of O_{E/Ξ}(−1), and their derived pushforwards vanish. The same holds with the horizontal compact-support twist.
hypotheses: The center is a smooth boundary stratum of the zero/pole intersection as in Yu §4(b); this is not a statement for arbitrary blowups with no boundary condition.
proofSteps: Write the two affine blowup charts, the transformed zero/pole divisors and their multiplicities.
Insert the intermediate complexes R^λ(q) with their exceptional pole bounds; compute the quotient of pullback and R^λ and the adjacent quotients.

Use the local exponential Koszul exactness to reduce them to relative O_E(−μ) with 0<μ≤dim_Ξ E on the projective-bundle exceptional divisor (requested from AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry:R09.7), whose fibre cohomology vanishes by SF.2/projective-space-cohomology. The projection formula (SF.2/derived-pullback-pushforward-qcoh) gives the compact variant.

nodes.title: Model independence and Deligne comparison
nodes.statement: For any two good compactifications, the image filtrations on H^r_dR(U,E^f) and its compact variant agree under their canonical de Rham identifications, because on each of them the image filtration equals the intrinsic F_irr of P/pair-fibre. On non-degenerate compactifications the same filtration is obtained before resolving indeterminacy. These filtrations equal F_irr of P/pair-cohomology. Their spectral sequences degenerate at E₁, so H^r(F^λ_log)→H^r(DR) is injective. The construction is functorial for the proper filtered direct images used to define pair cohomology.
hypotheses: Independence of the good model is deduced from the identification with F_irr on each model (ESY §1.7 and §3.4); Yu's own proof of Theorem 1.7 through weak factorization of birational maps is not used, and no weak-factorization input is required.

nodes.title: Newton filtration for a Laurent polynomial
nodes.statement: Let φ=Σ_m a_mx^m be a Laurent polynomial on T=(G_m)^n, Δ=conv({0}∪supp φ), and assume dim Δ=n. For every face σ not containing zero, require that the logarithmic derivatives x_i∂_iφ_σ have no common zero on T; this is Newton nondegeneracy. Define convenience by 0∈interior Δ. Let C_Δ be the cone generated by Δ and h(m)=inf{a≥0:m∈aΔ} on C_Δ. The cone Newton complex has qth term C[C_Δ∩Z^n]⊗Λ^q⟨dlog x_i⟩, differential d+dφ∧, and F^λ term zero for q<λ, otherwise the span of x^m dlog x_I with h(m)≤q−λ. Construct its comparison with the full Laurent twisted de Rham complex. The truncation by q≥λ is retained even at a cone containing lines.
hypotheses: Characteristic zero, full-dimensional Δ, and the face nondegeneracy test are explicit hypotheses for the comparison theorems.
In the nonconvenient case the cone can be smaller than R^n; do not replace its monoid by all Z^n.
proofSteps: Import character lattices, rational polytopes, fans and regular subdivisions from the toric supplier.
Use the gauge of the convex polytope to prove h is rational piecewise linear and subadditive; the exponents of φ have height at most one, so the displayed pole bound is stable under d+dφ.
Identify the finite filtration pieces with toric global sections of O(floor((q−λ)P)) via invariant divisor valuations; form the natural inclusion into the full Laurent complex.

nodes.title: Newton cohomology concentration and volume

The Newton spectral sequence degenerates at E₁.
hypotheses: This uses the graded semigroup-algebra acyclicity theorem of Adolphson–Sperber, whose full proof is recorded as gap G4.
Full dimension is necessary; a product torus on which φ is constant contributes ordinary torus cohomology.

For a top-form monomial x^m dlog x₁∧⋯∧dlog x_n from C_Δ, h(m)≤n−λ implies that its cohomology class lies in F^λ_irr. The equality of image filtrations holds independently of the toric subdivision and resolution of indeterminacy; it does not assert that all such monomials form an independent basis.

nodes.title: Constant boundary correction of a Laurent Gauss–Manin system
nodes.statement: For a convenient Newton-nondegenerate Laurent polynomial h:T=(G_m)^n→A¹, the cone of h_!pQ_T→h_*pQ_T has constant cohomology Hodge modules. Consequently ΠH⁰h_!pQ_T≅Π image(H⁰h_!pQ_T→H⁰h_*pQ_T)≅ΠH⁰h_*pQ_T. In particular the central pair compact-to-ordinary map is an isomorphism after Π and the central invariant is pure of exponential weight n. This is the complex Hodge-module analogue of the convenient boundary argument, with all operations normalized as in H.1.
hypotheses: Both convenience and face nondegeneracy are required.
The conclusion concerns a constant boundary cone; h need not be a proper morphism.
proofSteps: Take the closure of the graph h−θ=0 in a smooth proper toric refinement. Denef–Loeser’s face calculation gives a proper graph compactification smooth over the boundary strata, whose boundary maps have no vanishing cycles over A¹.

Use proper Betti base change, the local product charts and the boundary-strata Čech resolution to show every boundary direct-image cohomology is a local system on A¹. It is constant because A¹_an is simply connected.

Use the admissible fixed-part theorem (HodgeStructuresPartII H.2/mixed-fixed-part on the simply connected A¹) to upgrade underlying constant local systems to constant Hodge modules. The boundary localization triangle identifies these with the cone cohomology.
Apply exact Π, then the central weight result to its image.

sources.match: Gives the toroidal graph and local product boundary argument; its finite-field constancy step is replaced here by complex simple connectedness.
Uses the constant Gauss–Manin boundary correction and attributes the argument to Denef–Loeser.

nodes.title: Filtered Künneth and Poincaré duality
nodes.statement: For smooth quasi-projective pairs (U,f),(V,g), the ordinary Künneth isomorphism of P/pair-kunneth-duality identifies F^λ_irr on H^r(U×V,f⊞g) with ⊕_{a+b=r}Σ_{α+β=λ}F^α_irr H^a(U,f)⊗F^β_irr H^b(V,g). The same holds for compact supports. The perfect pairing H_c^r(U,f)⊗H^{2d−r}(U,−f)→C(−d) identifies the rational filtration with its dual: the annihilator of F^λ on the compact factor is F^{>d−λ} on the ordinary factor. Here F^{>a}=Σ_{b>a}F^b. These are constant-coefficient pair statements; no unrestricted irregular Hodge-module category is assumed.
hypotheses: Use the rational filtration from N/model-independence and actual pole multiplicities.
proofSteps: Starting from two good models, blow up intersections of boundary components whose f and g pole-order differences have opposite signs. The smallest negative product increases after finitely many such blowups, producing a non-degenerate model for f⊞g (CY §3.1).

On an intermediate model use the convex sum of divisor sheaves Σ_{0≤θ≤1}O(floor(μ((1−θ)P_f+θP_g))). On the initial product it is the convolution-filtered log complex. On each blowup its quotient is a sum of relative exceptional O(−1), hence has zero derived pushforward (projective-bundle structure of the exceptional divisor requested from AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry R09.7, and SF.2/projective-space-cohomology). Check the finite monomial-generator intersection resolution to justify pushforward even though that sum need not be locally free (CY §3.2).

Use the coherent external-product calculation (Künneth over C from SF.2/tor-independent-base-change and the projection formula, computed by Čech complexes, SF.2/cech-to-cohomology) and E₁ degeneration of both factors to identify the convolution filtration on hypercohomology, then transfer by N/model-independence. This is the additional filtered Künneth proof, rather than an appeal to the unfiltered formula.

For duality pair the log complex and its horizontal-boundary compact twist; local residue and Serre duality (SF.2/serre-proper) identify the complementary pole quotients, with the strict inequality at a rational jump. Apply filtered strictness and the trace. Obtain compact Künneth by dualizing the ordinary statement.
